newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee sales fall 2.5 pct in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee sales fall 2.5 pct in latest week.

text.p: The volume of Uganda coffee sales contracted in the week to November 15 fell by 2.5 percent to 69,400 60-kg bags compared to 71,250 bags in the week to November 8, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority said on Wednesday.

It said in a report that the bulk of contracts in the two weeks involved the sale of robusta Screen 15 (standard) grade, taking a share of 58.5 percent and 60.5 percent of the total contracts respectively.
Private exporters took a market share of 100 percent in the two weeks.
There was little activity in arabicas, which totalled only 4,800 bags in the first week and only 100 bags in the second week, due to the crop cycle in arabica growing areas.

"The slightly lower activity could be attributed to a slump in the international prices whose opening position at the London market oscillated between $1,540 and $1,500 a tonne in the first week compared to $1,524 and $1,508 in the second week," the authority said.

"Similarly, on the New York market, the first closing position ranged between 127.35 U.S. cents and 117.25 cents per pound in the first week compared to 125.85 and 118.20 cents in the second week," it added.

"Generally, the two markets were characterised by persistent concerns about prompt supplies in the first week while they were seen lower in the second week on a technically driven market. The markets did not respond to the report on the drawdown of U.S. certified consumer stocks."
